category: tcp+udp tunnel for local game servers (hosted, Japan)

free_tier.stated: [translated] Headline: 'A game server you can use for free, without limits'. The feature list gives 'Free' and 'Unlimited' as separate items, and the mechanism section says: 'When you start the OwnServer Client, a dedicated secure tunnel is created between OwnServer and your computer, and a public address dedicated to your server is issued.'

egress.terms: [translated] 'A game server you can use for free, without limits', with 'Unlimited' as a feature heading. No byte figure, no rate, no session length.; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: [translated] 'OwnServer Client' is a per-OS desktop download; the page documents no API, no command line and no configuration file.
tooling: the vendor's own desktop client only (Windows, Linux x86_64/ARM, macOS Intel/Apple Silicon builds listed); no CLI flag, no API, no .conf
chaining: none while suspended; if it reopens it would be the only free Japanese host that publishes an arbitrary local TCP or UDP port without an account.
binding_note: Nothing binds: the service is suspended. The announcement dated 2026/04/06 says operation has stopped temporarily and no restart date is set.

identity_cost.detail: [translated] The documented flow is: download the OwnServer Client, download the game server program, start the OwnServer Client, play with friends. No account, email or payment step appears in it.

reliability_note: Suspended 2026-04-06 for stated stability and security problems; a client-side connection drop was patched with auto-reconnect in v0.10.0 (2025-04-20), which is the class of failure that preceded the suspension.
confidence_note: The suspension is a dated sentence on the vendor's own front page. The protocol claim (TCP and UDP) rests on the vendor's per-game page, which this reader saw only as a search snippet; a probe would settle both the protocol and whether the host still answers.

evidence.proved: [translated] '2026/04/06: we had been publishing the service on a trial basis, but because there are many problems with stability and security we are temporarily suspending provision of the service. The restart date is undecided.'
The front page lists 'Free' and 'Unlimited' as features and describes a client-created tunnel that issues a public address for the local game server.

notes: The live host answered twice with a transport failure (HTTP 530) on 2026-10-23, which establishes nothing about the origin the archived capture of 2026-04-14 is what the record rests on. The vendor's game-specific page (ownserver.kumassy.com/games/custom) was seen only as a search snippet saying it publishes any TCP or UDP service, hence ingress is recorded from that snippet and not from a page read. Country: Japan; the operator writes in Japanese and names Japanese consumer ISPs as the problem it solves. Two blocks, either decisive: suspended, and identity-free but client-locked.

extras.wg_detail: A closed-source desktop client issues a public address for a local server; it does not hand out a WireGuard configuration, and a user is the only documented way in.
extras.volume_stated: [translated] 'A game server you can use for free, without limits', with 'Unlimited' as a feature heading. No byte figure, no rate, no session length.
extras.transit_note: The vendor relays between the issued public address and the client's machine.
